events.title: Finance Bill 2024 Tabled in Parliament
events.detail: The National Treasury tabled the Finance Bill 2024, proposing tax hikes on bread, mobile money transfers, motor vehicles, and menstrual health products to help close a widening budget deficit. The bill quickly became the flashpoint for youth anger over the cost of living.

events.title: Gen Z-Led #RejectFinanceBill2024 Mobilization Begins
events.detail: A largely leaderless, youth-driven online campaign against the Finance Bill 2024 spread rapidly on X and TikTok, mobilizing what became Kenya's largest youth-led protest movement in decades and spreading from Nairobi to 35 of the country's 47 counties within days.

events.title: Rex Masai Becomes the Movement's First Fatality
events.detail: 29-year-old Rex Kanyike Masai was shot on Moi Avenue in Nairobi's CBD and bled to death, becoming the first confirmed protester killed during the Finance Bill demonstrations. Video showed a plainclothes officer firing into the fleeing crowd; more than a year later, IPOA's inquest still had not identified the shooter.

events.title: Protesters Storm and Torch Parliament
events.detail: After MPs voted 195-106 to pass the Finance Bill, thousands of demonstrators breached the parliamentary compound in Nairobi, setting part of the building ablaze while lawmakers were evacuated through underground tunnels. Police opened fire on the crowd, killing at least 19 people and wounding dozens on the single deadliest day of the 2024 wave.

events.title: Ruto Withdraws the Finance Bill
events.detail: Facing a death toll rights groups put above 20 (and later revised sharply upward), President William Ruto declined to sign the Finance Bill 2024 into law, telling the nation in a televised address: "I concede and therefore I will not sign the 2024 finance bill and it shall subsequently be withdrawn."

events.title: State Abductions of Protest Organizers Documented
events.detail: Families and rights groups began reporting masked, plainclothes officers abducting protest organizers and vocal critics off the streets in unmarked vehicles. KNCHR would go on to document 82 abduction/enforced-disappearance cases between June and December 2024 alone, with 26 people never accounted for.

events.title: Ruto Fires His Entire Cabinet
events.detail: Bowing to sustained street pressure, President Ruto dismissed all Cabinet Secretaries and the Attorney General, retaining only Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua and Prime CS Musalia Mudavadi, citing the need to "listen keenly to what the people of Kenya have said."

events.title: ODM Figures Join Ruto's 'Broad-Based' Cabinet
events.detail: Reshuffling his cabinet in the protests' aftermath, Ruto brought several Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) figures aligned with Raila Odinga into government, framing the move as national cohesion. Critics called it elite power-sharing that sidestepped Gen Z's substantive demands.

events.title: Deputy President Gachagua Removed by Impeachment
events.detail: The Senate voted 53-66 to uphold impeachment charges against Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, including gross constitutional violations, ethnically divisive politics, and threatening a judge, making him the first Kenyan DP removed via impeachment. Ruto nominated Kithure Kindiki, then Interior CS, as his replacement within hours.

events.title: Ruto and Raila Sign 'Broad-Based Government' MOU
events.detail: President Ruto and opposition veteran Raila Odinga formalized their political pact at a signing ceremony at Nairobi's KICC, cementing a UDA-ODM cooperation framework. A later TIFA poll found most Kenyans opposed the arrangement.

events.title: Ruto Apologizes to Gen Z
events.detail: At a National Prayer Breakfast event, President Ruto issued his first public apology to the youth movement, saying: "To our children, if there has been any misstep, we apologise." Many Gen Z voices dismissed the gesture as "too little, too late" without compensation or accountability for the dead and missing.

era: Wave Two: Ojwang, Anniversary & Saba Saba (2025)

events.title: Blogger Albert Ojwang Dies in Police Custody
events.detail: Teacher and blogger Albert Ojwang, arrested in Homa Bay after criticizing Deputy IG Eliud Lagat online, died hours after being transferred to Nairobi's Central Police Station. Police initially claimed he hit his head on a cell wall; a government pathologist later found severe head trauma, neck compression, and soft-tissue injuries consistent with assault.

events.title: Nationwide Protests Erupt Over Ojwang's Death
events.detail: News of Ojwang's death in custody triggered spontaneous protests in Nairobi and other towns, reviving Gen Z mobilization tactics from 2024 and reigniting demands for police accountability just weeks after Ruto's apology tour.

events.title: Fresh Clashes Injure Dozens Over Ojwang Case
events.detail: Renewed demonstrations over the Ojwang case turned violent, with police using tear gas and, per witnesses, live rounds against crowds; at least 11 people were injured in clashes across Nairobi.

events.title: Mask Vendor Boniface Kariuki Shot in the Head
events.detail: 22-year-old street vendor Boniface Kariuki was shot at point-blank range on Moi Avenue after allegedly raising his hands in surrender to police. The incident, captured on video, became a rallying symbol of the second wave; a police constable was later charged with his murder.

events.title: Deputy IG Eliud Lagat Steps Aside
events.detail: Amid mounting pressure over the Ojwang case, Deputy Inspector General Eliud Lagat announced he would step aside pending investigations, stating: "I have chosen to step aside from my role as Deputy Inspector General – Kenya Police Service until the investigations are complete."

events.title: First Anniversary Protests Turn Deadly Nationwide
events.detail: Thousands marked the one-year anniversary of the parliament storming with a near-total shutdown of Nairobi, Eldoret, Nyeri, Nakuru, Mombasa and Kisii. Amnesty Kenya verified 16 killed and roughly 400 injured; broadcasters were ordered to halt live coverage.

events.title: Interior CS Murkomen Issues 'Shoot to Kill' Order
events.detail: A day after calling the unrest an attempted coup, Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen told police: "Na tumeambia polisi, mtu yeyote ambaye atakaribia police station, piga yeye risasi" ("We have told police, anyone who approaches a police station, shoot them"). The order triggered a court petition to have him declared unfit for office and a partial walk-back by Ruto, who told officers to "shoot in the leg, not to kill."

events.title: Boniface Kariuki Dies of His Wounds
events.detail: After three surgeries and being declared brain dead, mask vendor Boniface Kariuki succumbed to his gunshot wound at Kenyatta National Hospital, intensifying calls for President Ruto to resign.

events.title: Saba Saba 2025 Becomes the Deadliest Day Yet
events.detail: Protests coinciding with the 35th anniversary of Kenya's 1990 pro-democracy Saba Saba march turned into the single bloodiest day of the movement, with dozens killed as police fired live rounds and used water cannon. KNCHR's cumulative tally for June 2024 to July 2025 reached 115 deaths.

events.title: Activist Boniface Mwangi Arrested on Terrorism Charges
events.detail: Prominent activist Boniface Mwangi was arrested at his Lukenya, Machakos residence and accused of facilitating terrorism during the June 25 protests. The state dropped the terrorism charges days later, instead charging him with unlawful possession of ammunition; he pleaded not guilty on bail.

events.title: Opposition Icon Raila Odinga Dies at 80
events.detail: Former Prime Minister and longtime opposition leader Raila Odinga died of cardiac arrest while in India, reshaping Kenya's political landscape just as his ODM party's cooperation pact with Ruto faced growing public backlash. Kenya declared a public holiday and held a state funeral.

events.title: Amnesty Report Documents 128 Killed, 3,000 Arrested
events.detail: Amnesty International's comprehensive report on the movement's first 17 months found at least 128 people killed, roughly 3,000 arbitrary arrests, and 83 enforced disappearances, and documented how authorities used digital surveillance and internet disruptions to suppress organizing.

events.title: Telcos Warn of Steep Mobile-Money Tax Under Finance Bill 2026
events.detail: Kenyan telecom operators warned that combined excise duty, transaction fees, and a proposed 16% VAT on payment service providers in the Finance Bill 2026 could push the total cost burden on M-Pesa transfers from 15% to as high as 33.4%, reigniting cost-of-living anger ahead of the bill's passage.

events.title: Parliament Passes Finance Bill 2026, 122–40
events.detail: Despite an unprecedented wave of online public participation and objections to new levies on bread, betting winnings, banking charges and digital transactions, MPs passed the Finance Bill 2026 by a vote of 122 to 40, sending it to President Ruto for assent.

events.title: Ruto Signs Finance Bill 2026 Into Law Ahead of Anniversary
events.detail: President Ruto signed the Finance Bill 2026 into law at State House on June 23, days before the June 25 protest anniversary — the first time he assented to a Finance Bill before that date since taking office — while warning against any attempt to shut down the capital.

events.title: Government Begins First Compensation Payments to Protest Victims
events.detail: The Panel of Experts on Compensation of Victims of Human Rights Violations, chaired by Prof Makau Mutua, began disbursing the first phase of a KSh 2 billion reparations framework on June 23, 2026, releasing KSh 448.7 million to 348 verified victims of violations linked to protests and demonstrations between 2013 and 2025. Families of 115 people killed received KSh 3 million each (KSh 345 million total), while injury and other harm categories received amounts from KSh 200,000 to KSh 1 million. Mutua said compensation was issued only to victims who had given consent, the final procedural step before payment.

media.caption: Panel of Experts chair Prof Makau Mutua announces the first reparations payout to protest victims, June 23, 2026

events.title: Nairobi CBD Sealed Off for Second Anniversary Protests
events.detail: Police mounted roadblocks on every major route into Nairobi, cutting the capital off from the rest of the country ahead of the second anniversary of the parliament storming. Most CBD businesses stayed shut and more than 355 people were arrested nationwide.

events.title: Families Say Justice Still Elusive Two Years On
events.detail: On the second anniversary, families of protesters killed or forcibly disappeared since 2024 said investigations into their cases had stalled, with almost no officers convicted despite KNCHR and Amnesty documentation of scores of deaths and dozens of disappearances.

events.title: Mathare Protests Erupt Over Alleged Activist Abductions
events.detail: Demonstrations broke out in Nairobi's Mathare informal settlement after two local activists were allegedly abducted, resulting in at least one fatality and renewing fears that enforced disappearances had resumed under the 2026 wave.

events.title: Second Compensation Phase Clears KSh 225.4 Million for 157 More Victims
events.detail: The Panel of Experts on Compensation approved a second reparations phase on July 3, 2026, covering 157 additional victims — 100 injury cases and 57 fatalities — worth KSh 225.4 million. Families of the 57 deceased each received the standard KSh 3 million payout (KSh 171 million total), while injury compensation ranged from KSh 50,000 to KSh 1 million. The two phases combined brought cumulative disbursements to KSh 674.1 million across 505 victims, with more than 400 new claims filed within two weeks of a fresh call for victims to come forward.

media.caption: The second reparations phase brought cumulative payouts to KSh 674.1 million across 505 protest victims

events.title: Heavy Police Presence Suppresses Saba Saba 2026 March
events.detail: Organizers had notified police of a planned march of 1,000-3,000 people from Jeevanjee Gardens to Parliament for Saba Saba Day, demanding accountability for extrajudicial killings and disappearances. Police sealed off roads and swarmed the small group that managed to gather, with at least three people bundled into unmarked vehicles — a markedly smaller turnout than organizers had planned.

events.title: TIFA Poll: 52% of Kenyans Oppose Broad-Based Government
events.detail: A TIFA Research survey found 52% of Kenyans opposed the Ruto-Odinga broad-based government arrangement against just 30% in support, underscoring public skepticism that elite political pacts have addressed Gen Z's original grievances.

events.title: Activist Chains Himself to Police HQ Gates, Six Arrested Demanding IG Kanja's Resignation
events.detail: Activist Julius Kamau chained himself to the gates of Jogoo House, headquarters of Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, on August 17, 2026. He and five other activists carried white coffins reading "Why kill Kenyans?" and placards demanding Kanja's resignation over alleged police brutality, deaths in custody, and a renewed wave of abductions. Police unchained Kamau and arrested all six. Kamau, previously detained during Saba Saba 2026 and for disrupting Milimani High Court proceedings on missing persons, has become one of the movement's most visible individual agitators.

media.caption: Julius Kamau chained to the Jogoo House gate before his arrest, Aug 17, 2026

events.title: Ex-Chief Justice Maraga Gives Ruto 7-Day Ultimatum to Release Police Reforms Report
events.detail: Former Chief Justice David Maraga, who chaired the National Taskforce on Police Reforms, wrote to President Ruto on August 18, 2026 demanding release of the complete, unedited taskforce report submitted in November 2023, giving a seven-day deadline (August 25) and warning he would publish it himself if refused. Maraga said the government had for nearly three years failed to implement recommendations to restore the police service's independence and end brutality, accusing it of "organised political violence, goonism and partisan policing" in incidents spanning Homa Bay, Keumbu, Ol Kalou, Kisumu, Nairobi and Witima — which he characterized as "State Capture of the National Police Service."

media.caption: Former Chief Justice David Maraga and President William Ruto

events.title: Parliament Approves New IPOA Chairperson Amid Credentials Dispute
events.detail: The National Assembly approved Dr Duncan Ojwang Oburu's nomination as chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA) on August 19, 2026, succeeding Justice Ahmed Issack Hassan, who left after his appointment to the Court of Appeal. Ojwang, nominated by President Ruto in July, pledged during his August 12 vetting to "speak truth to power" and defend IPOA's independence, but legal experts raised concerns his qualifications may fall short of the High Court judge threshold the IPOA Act requires, with the committee moving to approve him despite the objections.

media.caption: Dr Duncan Ojwang Oburu before the National Assembly committee hearing, Aug 12, 2026

events.title: Gachagua Accuses Kindiki of Silence on Gen Z Crackdown Orders; Kindiki Fires Back
events.detail: Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua told Gen Z representatives he had personally challenged then-Interior CS Kithure Kindiki after a National Security Council meeting during the 2024 protests, alleging Kindiki privately agreed that orders to "abduct, torture and, where necessary, kill" protesters were wrong but declined to confront President Ruto over them. Now Deputy President, Kindiki rejected the claims as "petty lies," saying "Nobody will buy your petty lies. I told you I have been directed to kill people?" and countered he had been focused on counterterrorism and banditry at the time. The public feud reopens questions over senior officials' individual accountability for the 2024 crackdown that Gachagua's own October 2024 impeachment left unresolved.

media.caption: Deputy President Kithure Kindiki

events.title: Maraga's Report Deadline Expires as Ruto Unveils New Police Uniform Instead
events.detail: Former Chief Justice David Maraga's August 25 deadline for President Ruto to release the National Taskforce on Police Reforms report passed without the government publishing it or responding to his ultimatum. Two days later, Ruto announced he would personally unveil a redesigned police uniform at an August 28 passing-out parade for more than 6,000 constables at Kiganjo, with General Duty officers adopting it nationwide from August 31 — commentators noted the contrast between the swift uniform rollout and nearly three years of inaction on the substantive reforms report.

media.caption: President Ruto at a police passing-out parade, as the Maraga reforms report remains unpublished

events.title: Ruto Tells Katiba Day Symposium Gen Z Protests Were 'A Call to Be Heard'
events.detail: Speaking at the 16th Katiba Day Symposium at KICC marking the 2010 Constitution's anniversary, President Ruto said the 2024-2026 Gen Z protests represented citizens exercising constitutional freedoms rather than an assault on democracy, stating young Kenyans 'wanted to be heard.' He acknowledged lingering pain from crackdowns, said 'no Kenyan should lose their life, liberty or dignity for criticising the Government,' and called for every credible human-rights-violation allegation to be investigated independently and transparently — while still distinguishing peaceful protest from arson and looting, which he said the Constitution does not protect.

media.caption: President Ruto addresses the 16th Katiba Day Symposium at KICC, Aug 27, 2026

events.title: Nairobi Traders Shut Down CBD Over KRA Import Duty Hike, Police Fire Tear Gas
events.detail: Small-scale traders from Kamukunji, Gikomba, Eastleigh and Nyamakima marched through Moi Avenue and Luthuli Avenue toward the Kenya Revenue Authority's Times Towers offices on August 28, 2026, protesting a customs valuation benchmark hike for consolidated 40-foot containers from KSh 2.5 million to KSh 3.2 million. Police fired tear gas along Parliament Road and Kenyatta Avenue to disperse the crowd and blocked access to Times Towers and Parliament, closing hundreds of businesses. Traders said they would protest every Friday until KRA reverses the benchmark; the demonstration echoed the movement's core cost-of-living grievances even though organizers were not explicitly Gen Z-affiliated.

media.caption: Police fire tear gas at traders marching toward KRA's Times Towers offices, Nairobi CBD, Aug 28, 2026

events.title: Maraga Publicly Releases Long-Shelved Police Reforms Taskforce Report
events.detail: After President Ruto let his August 25 deadline expire without acting, former Chief Justice David Maraga made good on his ultimatum and publicly released the full National Taskforce on Police Reforms report on August 31, 2026 — nearly three years after handing it to Ruto in November 2023 — sharing a link to the complete document on his X account. Maraga said Kenyans have a right to scrutinise and debate a document produced with public resources, and that its central finding "is not a suggestion, it is a constitutional command: the National Police Service must be independent." The report calls for repealing 2014 amendments that gave the presidency outsized control over senior police appointments, restoring competitive and transparent recruitment for the Inspector-General and other top commanders, and ending tenure extensions beyond the statutory retirement age of 60. Maraga warned bluntly: "Unless the independence of the National Police Service is restored, we could soon have no country."

media.caption: Former Chief Justice David Maraga (file photo), who publicly released the police reforms taskforce report on Aug 31, 2026

events.title: Maraga Says Police Chiefs Kanja and Amin 'Occupy Office Illegally'
events.detail: Alongside releasing the full taskforce report on August 31, Maraga separately challenged the legality of the tenures of Inspector General Douglas Kanja and DCI Director Mohamed Amin, both of whom passed the statutory retirement age of 60 before their extensions. Citing Section 80 of the Public Service Commission Act 2017 — which limits extensions beyond 60 to cases involving rare skills unavailable elsewhere in the public service — Maraga said Kanja was appointed Inspector-General at age 61 without an open, competitive process, and argued both men 'occupy their offices illegally.' Kanja's appointment had previously been cleared by Parliament despite the same retirement-age objections being raised at the time.

media.caption: Former Chief Justice David Maraga, who says IG Douglas Kanja and DCI Director Mohamed Amin occupy their posts illegally past retirement age

events.title: Maraga Alleges Corruption in New Police Uniform Procurement
events.detail: Alongside releasing the full taskforce report, Maraga singled out the government's handling of its uniform-reform recommendation for criticism, saying "whereas police uniforms were part of the over 200 task force recommendations, the attempt to implement it [has] already been marred by corruption and opaqueness." The National Police Service said textile firm Bedi Investments Limited won the contract for the redesigned uniform Ruto unveiled on August 28 at Kiganjo, after four local manufacturers were invited to submit samples and only Bedi and Rivatex East Africa responded by the deadline. Maraga argued that swapping colors while leaving the taskforce's roughly 600 recommendations largely unimplemented amounted to a cosmetic fix that would not address the National Police Service's independence and accountability problems.

media.caption: President Ruto at the Aug 28 Kiganjo police uniform unveiling now under procurement scrutiny

events.title: Full Text Shows Taskforce Actually Recommended Reverting to Old Uniform
events.detail: The full taskforce document Maraga published on August 31 revealed that the National Taskforce on Police Reforms had recommended the National Police Service revert to its pre-2018 uniform for three years — following widespread complaints from officers and the public that the current attire failed to convey professionalism — before designing any replacement through a process with proper public and officer participation and formal gazettement. Ruto's August 28 unveiling of a newly redesigned uniform came less than three years after the report's November 2023 submission, meaning the rollout preempted the very consultation process the taskforce itself had prescribed.

media.caption: Former Chief Justice David Maraga, whose taskforce report revealed it had recommended keeping the old police uniform

events.title: Maraga Claims Nearly 4,000 Kenyans Killed by Police Since 2022
events.detail: Former Chief Justice David Maraga said police brutality had contributed to at least 3,958 deaths over President Ruto's first four years in office — an average of roughly 990 per year, or nearly three Kenyans killed daily by law enforcers. Maraga contrasted the figure with the Kibaki era (4,035 deaths over 10 years, about 404 per year) and the Uhuru Kenyatta era (4,150 deaths over 10 years, about 415 per year), arguing the annual rate under Ruto is more than double his predecessors' despite the taskforce report he chaired having been submitted nearly three years earlier. The government did not immediately dispute or respond to the specific figures.

media.caption: Former Chief Justice David Maraga cites a nearly four-year tally of over 3,900 police-linked deaths under President Ruto

events.title: Government Spokesperson Clarifies New Uniform Covers Only General-Duty Officers
events.detail: Facing criticism over the uniform's cost and the taskforce's contrary recommendation, Government Spokesperson Charles Owino said on the night of September 1 that the redesigned attire unveiled August 28 applies only to the roughly 60,000 general-duty officers seen on patrol and at police stations, not the entire National Police Service — the Administration Police and General Service Unit uniforms remain unchanged. Owino said the rollout would proceed in phases as existing kits wear out, starting with newly graduated recruits, and separately noted entry-level police pay had risen 36%, from KSh 20,390 to KSh 38,975 a month, as part of the broader reform package.

media.caption: Kenya's redesigned general-duty police uniform, whose rollout scope government spokesperson Charles Owino clarified on Sept 1

events.title: Amnesty Kenya: 19 Enforced Disappearances, 69 Police Killings So Far in 2026
events.detail: Marking the UN's International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances (August 30), Amnesty International Kenya said 19 people had been subjected to enforced disappearance in Kenya in 2026 so far — up sharply from 6 documented in all of 2025 — while police-linked killings stood at 69 for the year, down from 125 in 2025. New Executive Director George Morara said "words must now be matched with action," pointing to a June 2026 KNCHR reparations framework that verified 35 enforced-disappearance cases.

media.caption: Amnesty International Kenya's August 30, 2026 statement on enforced disappearances

events.title: Ruto Orders KRA to Reverse Container Customs Benchmark After Trader Shutdown
events.detail: Meeting MSME traders and cargo consolidators at State House on September 2, 2026 — five days after tear-gas clashes shut down parts of the Nairobi CBD — President Ruto directed the Kenya Revenue Authority to restore the consolidated 40-foot container customs valuation benchmark from KSh 3.2 million back to KSh 2.5 million, with later reporting indicating a further cut to KSh 2 million was planned. Ruto also ordered KRA to publish a list of high-value goods excluded from the consolidated-cargo arrangement, maintain a public register of authorized consolidators, and remove the Advance Cargo Declaration requirement. The reversal marked a rare rapid concession to a cost-of-living protest outside the core Gen Z movement.

media.caption: President William Ruto, who directed KRA to reverse the container customs benchmark hike after trader protests

events.title: Standard Group Editor Alex Kiprotich Abducted, Dumped Near Masinga Dam
events.detail: Standard Group Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich was forced from his vehicle by four masked men armed with AK-47 rifles on the Gilgil-Nakuru Road around 9:20pm on September 1, 2026, and questioned about his journalism and sources before being abandoned near Masinga Dam, roughly 230km away, around 3am. He was found safe but shaken; it was the second attack on him after a June 27, 2026 incident in which he evaded a similar roadside interception. KTN News suggested the attack could be linked to state elements seeking to intimidate Standard Group's critical coverage of the Ruto administration. Interior CS Murkomen called the incident "embarrassing and barbaric," ordered an investigation, and assigned it to a newly created Anti-Abduction Unit.

media.caption: Security response following the abduction of Standard Group editor Alex Kiprotich, Sept 2026

events.title: Murkomen Denies 'Parallel Police Command' Amid Abduction Claims
events.detail: Addressing the 59th Passing-Out Parade of Administration Police Service recruits at the National Police College, Embakasi on September 4, 2026, Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen rejected suggestions — sharpened by the Kiprotich abduction and Amnesty's disappearance tally — that any unit within the National Police Service operates outside Inspector General Douglas Kanja's command, calling such claims "false propagandists." He said Article 245 of the Constitution protects the IG's command independence over investigations, promotions and deployment. President Ruto separately defended his administration's record on implementing the Maraga taskforce's police-reform recommendations while addressing GSU graduates at Embakasi the following day.

media.caption: Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen addresses APS recruits at Embakasi, Sept 4, 2026

events.title: Panel of Experts' Term Extended 90 Days as Payouts Reach KSh 896.1M
events.detail: President Ruto extended the term of the Panel of Experts on Compensation of Victims of Human Rights Violations by a further 90 days effective September 4, 2026, via Gazette Notice No. 14149. Chaired by Prof Makau Mutua with KNCHR chairperson Claris Awuor Ogangah-Onyango as vice-chair, the panel had by August 2026 processed 680 legitimate claims and disbursed KSh 896.1 million to beneficiaries — up from the 505 victims and KSh 674.1 million reported after the second payout phase in July. It was the panel's third extension since being reconstituted in January 2026 following a High Court ruling on its mandate.

media.caption: Panel of Experts chair Prof Makau Mutua (file photo)

events.title: Taskforce Report Exposes Police Recruitment Bribery Racket
events.detail: Reporting on the newly public taskforce document, The Star detailed the report's findings on National Police Service recruitment: complaints of corruption were received from all 47 counties, with job slots reportedly sold for up to KSh 600,000. The unedited report found recruitment routinely driven by "corruption, cronyism, nepotism and political influence" rather than merit, with slots sold to those who can pay or given to relatives of powerful, politically connected figures, and officers who entered through political patronage sustaining their positions by staying loyal to their patrons.

media.caption: Former Chief Justice David Maraga, whose taskforce report also documented widespread bribery in police recruitment
